picks.excerpt: Epic's Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 session on 'World Modeling and Vibe Simulation with Unreal Engine' shows how engine-authored scenes become promptable synthetic-data and simulation pipelines for physical-AI systems. A concrete look at world models entering a mainstream production engine rather than staying in demo reels.
picks.rationale: The only production-tooling story in the pool: world models moving into a mainstream engine changes what an authored scene is actually for.

picks.excerpt: After its Soulslike landed at 25% positive on Steam, the developer publicly concedes players read AI-assisted assets as an absence of effort: 'if it looks like the effort is not there, that is a fair reading of what is on screen.' A blunt account of perceived craft becoming the actual quality bar.
picks.rationale: A developer on the record admitting perceived effort is the real quality bar — the clearest statement yet of the cost of AI-assisted assets at retail.

picks.excerpt: The retro revival James Pond's new trailer set off AI alarm bells among viewers — comments were turned off — and the developer insists no generative AI was used. A case study in how AI-detection suspicion now shapes marketing art direction whether or not AI was involved.
picks.rationale: The false-positive case: suspicion now attaches to human-made work too, which makes art direction a reputation decision even without AI in the pipeline.

picks.excerpt: The 20-year-old shooter Gunz the Duel returned to Steam to a mixed rating, with players flagging suspected generative-AI art in the re-release alongside network problems. Another case of AI-asset detection by the audience turning into an immediate storefront-reputation hit.
picks.rationale: Shows the same detection dynamic hitting a re-release, where AI-looking art compounds ordinary launch problems into a mixed store rating.

picks.excerpt: Sony's CEO argues that as AI-generated content floods creative fields, audiences will increasingly seek out demonstrably human-made work — a strategic bet from a platform holder whose studios set art-direction norms. Frames 'human-made' as a positioning asset rather than a constraint.
picks.rationale: A platform holder framing 'human-made' as market positioning rather than nostalgia — the strategic counterpart to the backlash cases above.
